mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, indicating supply chain disruptions, will lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle to meet demand and earnings estimates are revised downward.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 50% of months following a 1%+ m/m drop in IP.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected spike in the unemployment rate, signaling a rapidly weakening labor market, will trigger a risk-off sentiment and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day SPX returns are positive in > 40% of instances following a 0.3pp+ m/m rise in UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts and retail sales both show signs of weakening, indicating a broad-based slowdown in consumer demand, S&P 500 returns will be negative over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline y/y
failure_condition: 20-day SPX returns are positive in > 55% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS show y/y declines.

mechanism_narrative: A surprise interest rate hike by the Fed, indicating a more aggressive tightening cycle, will lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the higher cost of capital pressures equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25pp in a single meeting
failure_condition: 20-day SPX returns are positive in > 50% of instances following a 0.25pp+ rate hike.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate is low and falling, indicating a tight labor market, wage pressures will build and eventually lead to higher inflation, causing the Fed to tighten policy and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: CPI inflation remains below 2% y/y over the 60-day signal period, indicating that wage pressures are not spilling over into consumer prices.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP growth is strong and accelerating, but inflation remains low, the Fed is likely to maintain an accommodative policy stance, boosting equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 3% y/y and CPIAUCSL < 2% y/y
failure_condition: Fed funds rate rises > 0.5pp over the 20-day signal period, indicating that the Fed is not maintaining an accommodative stance.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production is rising rapidly, indicating strong supply chain momentum, companies will be able to meet consumer demand more easily, reducing inflation pressures and allowing the Fed to maintain a more accommodative policy stance, boosting S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: CPI inflation rises > 0.5pp over the 60-day signal period, indicating that supply chain momentum is not containing price pressures.
